newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria approves sale of 51 pct of cement plant.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria approves sale of 51 pct of cement plant.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government has approved the sale of 51 percent of Beloizvorski Ziment cement plant to Swiss group Holderbank for $32.5 million, Construction Minister Nikola Karadimov said on Monday.
"The construction ministry and the potential buyer Holderbank have agreed $32.5 million for 51 percent of Beloizvorski Ziment," he told reporters.
The buyer is to pay $21.5 million of the price in cash and the rest in Bulgarian Brady bonds or domestic bad debt bonds.

Swiss building materials group Holderbank Financiere Glarus AG is also to invest $16.6 million in the plant over the next three years, which would not be considered an increase of its stake, said Karadimov.
Another $14.4 million should be invested by the buyer eight years later.
Bulgaria would retain a 49 percent stake in Beloizvorski Ziment.
Karadimov declined to say whether Beloizvorski Ziment had outstanding debts to the budget or commercial banks.

"We will try this week to sign a preliminary contract with the buyer we have chosen. We will seek that the buyer deposits in advance a certain sum to guarantee its commitment to the deal," Karadimov said.
The final contract could be signed after parliament, which assembles after the April 19 election, approves the government's decision to offer the buyer concession rights on the adjacent lime quarry.
The Swiss company was chosen by the government after negotiations with four bidders, Karadimov said.
